```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
ROOT <- "/users/4/coffm049/papers/functionalBrainHerit"
# For local render (Windows) the same relative paths work; ROOT not needed for images
WIDE <- file.path(ROOT, "results/summary/mash_twin_wide.csv")
wide <- read_csv(WIDE, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Detect which SNP columns are available. AdjHE-FE is the reported SNP method
# for all three phenotype sets (SA via SA/AdjHE_FE_wo_total.json); fall back to
# AdjHE-RE when an FE stream has not been run yet.
gordon_col <- if ("h2_gordon_AdjHE_FE" %in% names(wide)) "h2_gordon_AdjHE_FE" else "h2_gordon_AdjHE_RE"
proba_col  <- if ("h2_proba_AdjHE_FE"  %in% names(wide)) "h2_proba_AdjHE_FE"  else "h2_proba_AdjHE_RE"
sa_col     <- if ("h2_SA_AdjHE_FE"     %in% names(wide)) "h2_SA_AdjHE_FE"     else "h2_SA_AdjHE_RE"

gordon_label <- if (gordon_col == "h2_gordon_AdjHE_FE") "AdjHE-FE" else "AdjHE-RE"
proba_label  <- if (proba_col  == "h2_proba_AdjHE_FE")  "AdjHE-FE" else "AdjHE-RE"
sa_label     <- if (sa_col     == "h2_SA_AdjHE_FE")     "AdjHE-FE" else "AdjHE-RE"

# Image path suffixes
gordon_img_sfx <- if (gordon_col == "h2_gordon_AdjHE_FE") "AdjHE" else "AdjHERE"
proba_img_sfx  <- if (proba_col == "h2_proba_AdjHE_FE") "AdjHE" else "AdjHERE"
# Manhattan panels use literal method names (Twin / AdjHEFE / AdjHERE),
# one figure per atlas x method, all sharing the SNP-ordered x-axis. GCTA
# figures are still written by 05_manhattan.py but are not shown: GCTA
# zero-censors >50% of FC edges and has no flag column, so it is not
# comparable to the AdjHE panels (see 01_compare_mash_twin.R).

fivenum_tbl <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x)==0) return(tibble(min=NA, q1=NA, median=NA, mean=NA, q3=NA, max=NA, n=0, sd=NA))
  tibble(
    min = min(x), q1 = quantile(x, 0.25), median = median(x),
    mean = mean(x), q3 = quantile(x, 0.75), max = max(x),
    n = length(x), sd = sd(x)
  )
}
# Helper to filter n=0 rows for publication (per user: filter all tables to remove n=0)
filter_n0 <- function(df) {
  if ("n" %in% names(df)) df <- df %>% filter(n != 0)
  if ("n_valid" %in% names(df)) df <- df %>% filter(n_valid != 0)
  if ("n_networks" %in% names(df)) df <- df %>% filter(n_networks != 0)
  if ("n_pheno" %in% names(df)) df <- df %>% filter(n_pheno != 0)
  df
}
```

## Estimation and quality control of the SNP heritability estimates

All SNP heritabilities were estimated with the MASH estimator (MASH
`ffb888d`). Two AdjHE variants are reported for every phenotype set and they are
**not** the same computation: they differ in whether collection site enters as a
random effect, and consequently they use different solvers and — importantly for
how the results should be read — different failure detection.

### Solver selected by site handling

`AdjHE(...)` dispatches on `random_groups` (`AdjHE.py:12`):

- **AdjHE-FE** (`random_groups: null`; `abcd_site` in `covar_discrete`) takes the
  **two-component** path, `_adjhe_2comp`, which returns `sigma_g` and `sigma_e`
  with no site component.
- **AdjHE-RE** (`random_groups: "abcd_site"`) takes the **three-component** path,
  `_adjhe_3comp`, which additionally estimates a site variance `sigma_s`.

Both paths standardise the phenotype, restrict the GRM to rows with non-missing
phenotype, and project out the first `npc = 20` principal components using
`Q = I - V(V'V)^{-1}V'` with `V` from a QR factorisation of the PC columns. The
projection is applied to the traces only, not materialised. Projected quantities
are `tr(AQ) = tr(A) - tr(V'AV)`, `tr(AQA) = tr(A^2) - 2tr((AV)'(AV)) +
tr(V'AVAV)`, and the effective sample size is reduced to `n_adj = n - npc`.

### Two-component path (AdjHE-FE)

Variance components are obtained in closed form from the projected traces:

$$\hat\sigma_g = \frac{(y'A_Qy)\,n_{adj} - \mathrm{tr}(A_Q)\,y'Q_{y}y}{\Delta}, \qquad
\hat\sigma_e = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(A_QA_Q)\,y'Q_{y}y - \mathrm{tr}(A_Q)\,(y'A_Qy)}{\Delta}$$

with

$$\Delta = \mathrm{tr}(A_QA_Q)\, n_{adj} - \big[\mathrm{tr}(A_Q)\big]^2 .$$

**Degeneracy criterion.** A non-positive or non-finite `Delta` is flagged
`nonpos_det` and all variance components are returned as `NaN`. This is a
*determinant sign test on a 2x2 system*, and it is the only degeneracy screen on
this path — **no condition number is computed for AdjHE-FE at any `npc` or sample
size.** A finite `Delta > 0` guarantees a non-singular 2x2 solve, but says
nothing about whether the estimate is well determined.

### Three-component path (AdjHE-RE) and the near-singularity condition

The site component is `S = blockdiag(1_{n_1}, ..., 1_{n_G}) = DD'`, where `D` is
the site indicator matrix. With `QSQ` computed explicitly and `yy' = y y'`, the
3x3 cross-product (normal-equations) matrix and moment vector are

$$X_tX = \begin{pmatrix}
\mathrm{tr}(A^2) & \mathrm{tr}(QSQA) & \mathrm{tr}(A)\\
\mathrm{tr}(QSQA) & \mathrm{tr}(QSQQSQ) & \mathrm{tr}(QSQ)\\
\mathrm{tr}(A) & \mathrm{tr}(QSQ) & n
\end{pmatrix}, \qquad
X_ty = \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{tr}(A\,yy')\\[2pt] \mathrm{tr}(QSQ\,yy')\\[2pt] \mathrm{tr}(yy')\end{pmatrix}.$$

**Near-singularity condition.** The 2-norm condition number of this matrix is
evaluated before solving,

$$\kappa = \mathrm{cond}_2(X_tX) = \sigma_{\max}(X_tX) / \sigma_{\min}(X_tX),$$

and the estimate is rejected when

$$\kappa > 10^{10} \quad\text{or}\quad \kappa \notin \mathbb{R},$$

flagged `ill_conditioned`, with all three variance components returned as `NaN`.
Two adjacent guards follow: `numpy.linalg.LinAlgError` raised by the solve is
flagged `singular`, and a `NaN` anywhere in the solved components is flagged
`nan_solve`. The `10^{10}` threshold is hardcoded in `AdjHE.py:154` and is not
configurable from the pipeline: no argument file in this repository carries a
conditioning or tolerance parameter.

**Why the threshold exists.** The conditioning check was not precautionary. An
earlier revision projected the site indicators out along with the PCs. Because
`S` is built from that same site indicator matrix, `QD = 0`, so

$$QSQ = QD\,D'Q = (QD)(QD)' = \mathbf{0}$$

identically: the middle row and column of `X_tX` were exactly zero, `kappa` was
infinite for **every** phenotype, `npc` and sample size, and 100% of RE rows were
flagged `ill_conditioned`. The fix (`ffb888d`) restricts the projection to the PC
columns only — a component estimated as a random effect has no business being
projected away as a fixed effect — and `MASH/tests/test_adjhe_site_projection.py`
regression-tests that RE no longer returns `ill_conditioned` at any `npc` or `N`.
The `10^{10}` cut-off therefore encodes "collinear enough that the solve is
meaningless", not a data-driven threshold.

### Post-solve screening, common to both paths

`h2 = sigma_g / (sigma_g + sigma_e)`, then:

- `sigma_g < 0` → flag `neg_sigma_g`;
- `h2 < 0` → clamp to 0 and flag `h2_neg_clamped` (near-zero heritability or poor fit);
- `h2 > 1` → **return `NaN`** and flag `h2_gt_1_invalid`. This is deliberately *not*
  clamped to 1, because a variance ratio above 1 signals a collapsed solve (typically
  `sigma_e ~ 0`) and clamping would masquerade as perfect heritability.

Flags compound (`"neg_sigma_g;h2_neg_clamped"`), so the pipeline's filter matches
on substrings; the vocabulary is centralised in `summary/mash_flags.R`.

The variance of `h2` is computed as `2n / (n tr(A^2) - tr(A)^2)` from the
**unprojected** traces. If that denominator is non-positive the variance is
replaced by its absolute value and logged, but **not** flagged — a degenerate
`var(h2)` therefore survives into the output with `flag = "ok"`. We exclude no
rows on `var(h2)` alone.

### GCTA and HEreg are not screened at all

**No equivalent condition is applied to GCTA or HEreg, because none exists in
the code.** Only `AdjHE.py` emits a `flag` column; `GCTA_wrapper.py` and
`two_step_M_est.py` compute no condition number, catch no `LinAlgError`, and
their output schema has no `flag` field. A GCTA row that failed, or was
ill-conditioned, or returned a negative variance clamped at zero is
**indistinguishable from a genuine estimate of zero**. There is likewise no
`ill_conditioned` equivalent to search for, and the absence of such a flag in a
GCTA stream is not evidence of good conditioning.

To keep the summarised distributions on comparable footing, the pipeline
therefore substitutes a **sign filter**: for streams with no `flag` column
(GCTA, HEreg) any row with `h2 <= 0` is dropped. This is a sign test, not a
conditioning screen — it removes clamped negatives but cannot detect a
well-conditioned solve that is nonetheless unreliable. This is why GCTA returns
`h2 = 0` for a large fraction of FC edges and is excluded from the panels below.

### Consequence for interpreting the FE/RE contrast

The two reported AdjHE variants are **not symmetric in failure detection**:

| | degeneracy screen | can emit |
|---|---|---|
| AdjHE-FE | determinant sign test `Delta <= 0` | `nonpos_det`, `neg_sigma_g`, `h2_neg_clamped`, `h2_gt_1_invalid` |
| AdjHE-RE | `cond2(X_tX) > 1e10` | `ill_conditioned`, `singular`, `nan_solve`, `neg_sigma_g`, `h2_neg_clamped`, `h2_gt_1_invalid` |

A retained AdjHE-FE row has had **no conditioning check applied to it at all**,
whereas a retained AdjHE-RE row has been explicitly conditioned-screened. The
retained fractions therefore differ by construction (~48% FE vs ~77% RE for
Gordon; ~37% vs ~75% for ProbaConns; 13 of 18 for both SA variants), and the
panels are drawn on a shared x-axis with their own `n` printed. Differences in
median `h2` between the FE and RE panels should be read as differences in both
the estimator *and* the subset of phenotypes that survived screening, not as a
method contrast alone.

# Summary {.scrollable style="text-align:center;"}

::: {style="overflow-y:auto; max-height:820px; text-align:left; font-size:1.15em; line-height:1.6;"}

- **low FC heritability mostly within networks:** median SNP h² `r sprintf("%.4f", median(wide[[gordon_col]][wide$Set == "gordon" & !is.na(wide[[gordon_col]])]))` (Gordon, `r gordon_label`); Twin median is 0.177 within vs 0.119 across networks
- **Surface area h2 higher:** SA Twin mean h² is 0.177, reaching ~0.401 in MTL and VIS
- **Twin–SNP gap:** Gordon mean h² is `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(wide$Twin_h2[wide$Set == "gordon" & !is.na(wide$Twin_h2)]))` (Twin) vs `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(wide[[gordon_col]][wide$Set == "gordon" & !is.na(wide[[gordon_col]])]))` (SNP, `r gordon_label`) — standard missing heritability gap. Both values are computed from `wide` rather than hardcoded: the retained SNP median moved by ~17× when the Gordon AdjHE-FE stream was re-run with `abcd_site` as a fixed effect, and a hardcoded figure did not notice.
- **h2 changes with distance:** Gordon Twin h2 decreases with distance across networks ($\rho$ = −0.104) but increases within networks (R = 0.103).
- **Zero-heritability common:** 14.1% of across- and 7.9% of within-network connections sit at zero (h2 ≤ 1e-9, Gordon Twin).

:::

## Gordon — Five-Number Summaries & Correlations

```{r gordon-stats}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 5

gordon_wide <- wide %>% filter(Set=="gordon")
# Twin vs SNP comparison for fivenum
gordon_long <- gordon_wide %>%
  select(Pheno, Twin_h2, all_of(gordon_col)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Twin_h2, all_of(gordon_col)), names_to="Method", values_to="h2") %>%
  mutate(Method = recode(Method, Twin_h2="Twin", !!gordon_col := gordon_label))
# fivenum per Method — filter n=0 (per user)
fivenum_gordon <- gordon_long %>%
  group_by(Method) %>% summarise(fivenum_tbl(h2), .groups="drop") %>% filter(n != 0) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x,3)))
kable(filter_n0(fivenum_gordon), caption="Gordon — h2 five-number summary (Twin vs `r gordon_label`, 20 PCs)")
```

```{r gordon-corr}
corr <- read_csv(file.path(ROOT,"results/summary/correlations_by_set.csv"), show_col_types=FALSE) %>% filter(Set=="gordon")
corr <- corr %>% filter(n != 0)
# Only Pearson R per user (remove Spearman/R2)
corr <- corr %>% select(any_of(c("Set","MashMethod","n","Pearson_r"))) %>% mutate(Pearson_r = round(Pearson_r, 3))
kable(filter_n0(corr), caption="Gordon — Twin vs MASH Pearson R")
```

### Gordon — Within vs Outside Network h2 (10th, 50th, 90th)

```{r gordon-within-outside}
wo_path <- file.path(ROOT, "results/summary/within_outside_h2.csv")
```

## SA-FC System Correlation — FC parcel-mean / 90th percentile / within-system h2 vs SA h2

```{r sa-fc-corr}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
corr_path <- file.path(ROOT, "results/summary/sa_fc_h2_correlation.csv")
corr_sa_fc <- read_csv(corr_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
# Wide format: one column per method (Twin, AdjHE-FE, AdjHE-RE), drop n_networks
corr_sa_fc <- corr_sa_fc %>% filter(n_networks != 0)
corr_wide <- corr_sa_fc %>%
  select(any_of(c("atlas","method","metric","sa_type","pearson_r"))) %>%
  mutate(pearson_r = round(pearson_r, 3)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = pearson_r) %>%
  arrange(match(atlas, c("gordon","probaConns")), match(metric, c("fc_mean","fc_p90","fc_within","fc_outside")), sa_type)
# Order columns Twin then the reported SNP method (AdjHE-FE for all atlases)
mcols <- intersect(c("Twin","AdjHE-FE","AdjHE-RE"), names(corr_wide))
corr_wide <- corr_wide %>% select(any_of(c("atlas","metric","sa_type")), all_of(mcols))
kable(corr_wide, caption="SA-FC h2 by system: Pearson R of FC parcel-mean / p90 / within / outside h2 vs SA h2 (14 nets; rows = atlas × metric × SA type; SNP = AdjHE-FE for all atlases, falling back to AdjHE-RE where no FE run exists)")
```

```{r sa-fc-scatter}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
# SA h2 (x) vs FC within-system / outside-system h2 (y) per network — within vs across w.r.t. SA
detail_path <- file.path(ROOT, "results/summary/sa_fc_per_network.csv")
det <- read_csv(detail_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
det_long <- det %>% select(any_of(c("atlas","method","sa_type","network","sa_h2","fc_within","fc_outside"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(fc_within, fc_outside), names_to = "metric", values_to = "fc_h2") %>%
  mutate(metric = recode(metric, fc_within = "within-system", fc_outside = "outside-system")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(sa_h2), is.finite(fc_h2))
p <- ggplot(det_long, aes(x = sa_h2, y = fc_h2, color = metric)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(method ~ atlas) +
  labs(x = "SA h2 per network", y = "FC h2 per network", color = "FC edges") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
print(p)
```

```{r fc-dist-within-across}
# h2 vs distance, split within (same_network TRUE) vs across (FALSE) — per atlas × method
dist_path <- file.path(ROOT, "results/summary/fc_distance_per_edge.csv")
dd <- read_csv(dist_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
dd <- dd %>% mutate(group = if_else(same_network, "within", "across"))
dist_sum <- dd %>% group_by(atlas, method, group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(is.finite(h2)),
    n_zero = sum(h2 <= 1e-9, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_zero = 100 * mean(h2 <= 1e-9, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_h2 = mean(h2, na.rm = TRUE),
    p10_h2 = quantile(h2, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    p50_h2 = quantile(h2, 0.50, na.rm = TRUE),
    p90_h2 = quantile(h2, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_nz = suppressWarnings(median(h2[h2 > 1e-9], na.rm = TRUE)),
    mean_euclid = mean(euclidean_dist, na.rm = TRUE),
    pearson_h2_euclid = suppressWarnings(cor(h2, euclidean_dist, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")),
    pearson_h2_geodesic = suppressWarnings(cor(h2, geodesic_dist, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n != 0) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3)))
kable(filter_n0(dist_sum), caption="FC h2 vs distance — within (same network) vs across: n, n_zero/pct_zero (h2<=1e-9), mean/p10/p50/p90 h2, median of h2>1e-9, mean Euclidean, Pearson R(h2, Euclidean) and R(h2, geodesic). Pearson is attenuated by zero-inflation — compare median_nz vs p50.")
```

## Percent SNP Heritability of Twin Estimates — `100 × SNP / Twin` per Phenotype Set (SNP = AdjHE-FE for all sets)

```{r percent-snp}
pct_path <- file.path(ROOT, "results/summary/percent_SNP_explained.csv")
pct <- read_csv(pct_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 2)))
# Filter n=0
pct <- filter_n0(pct)
# Keep Set order gordon, probaConns, SA; select only needed cols for display (keep Pearson focus but percent table is separate)
pct <- pct %>% arrange(match(Set, c("gordon","probaConns","SA")))
# Only show mean/median + SE for publication (keep full for now but ensure n_valid !=0)
kable(pct, caption="Percent SNP heritability of Twin estimates — 100 × SNP / Twin per phenotype (per Set: mean ± SE, median, SD, q1/q3, min/max, n_valid; SNP = AdjHE-FE for all sets; SA 14 nets excl. 4/6/17, FCs filtered Twin_h2>0.001, MASH 0–1.2)")
cat("\n\n*Interpretation: `mean_pct` = mean of per-phenotype `pct`; `se_pct = sd / sqrt(n_valid)`; `median_pct` robust to outliers (Twin near 0 inflates mean). `ratio_of_means_pct = 100 × mean(MASH)/mean(Twin)` is also shown.*\n")
```
